areas.justification: The deployment table names an industrial Linux SMP gateway and the excluded list is explicit, but §1.2 states the application is proposed and not user-confirmed and §1.4 values are proposals.
Eleven FEAT rows each map to a requirement; only the deferred ACE configurations blur the scope.
Coherence, CMO and FENCE.I are specified down to phases and error order, and DEC-043 closes the circular wait, but fairness of the atomic claim and the directory sizing are open.
AXI4, AWATOP and AXI4-Lite contracts are declared with deviations, but the external interrupt to CVA6 mapping and PPROT policy are not specified.
One synchronous clock and a coordinated reset contract are clear; reset used as handshake data, WFI and clock gating versus probes, and reset-only fatal recovery are not governed.
§8.1 bounds every parameter, but profile 2 and the internal directory switch are missing from it and no elaboration-time legality check exists.
§9 gives widths, encodings and truncation for every quantity; only the profile-dependent PMU skew is undefined.
The acceptance target in DEC-045 is not reachable by the measured design and the directory has no macro-replaceable storage boundary.
§17 has no clock period, no I/O budget and no exception, while the real flow uses 1.04167 ns with 40 percent I/O delays.
No area or power proxy is stated although synthesis shows the directory at 56 percent of the logic area; REQ-PD-001 defers all numbers.
§13 lists cases and formulas but no cycle, latency or throughput value, and the profiles add latency without a number.
The workbook and the §11.2 flow are usable; there is no version or configuration register and no hart start control.
§16 delegates scan, MBIST and ATPG to the SoC; the top has no test port and the LLC test enable is tied to zero.
No ECC or parity decision, PPROT policy open, reset-only fatal recovery and no timeouts; no safety claim is made.
61 tests are traced, but there are no named properties, no coverage threshold and the OPEN-DV areas hid real defects.
Identifiers, decisions and a traceability matrix exist; REQ-PERF-007 is untraced, 31 open items carry no owner or date and the document is 9.7k lines.
Contracts exist in many sections; no single integration checklist lists the SoC obligations.
Coherent multicore with a shared LLC is in line with commercial Linux clusters, but I/O coherence, L2 ECC and a frequency claim are missing.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: Acceptance target is unreachable by the measured design
findings.detail: DEC-045 requires timing checks at 1.25 ns and 1.04167 ns while DEC-044 forbids any change to the CVA6 pipeline; the synthesis report of dual_gf55_800.zip shows a 3.40 ns critical path of 46 cells (WNS -2.47 ns, 312,168 failing endpoints) and the CVA6 internals alone sit at about 3.4 ns.
findings.action: Replace the fixed targets by a period sweep (2.0 to 3.5 ns) and record the accepted period per corner; separate the PPA target from the timing-profile mechanism.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: No interface timing budget or executable constraint in the specification
findings.detail: §17.1 says no SDC can be written and leaves the period and I/O delays to the SoC, but the flow uses create_clock 1.04167 ns, 1 percent uncertainty and 0.4167 ns input and output delay, which leaves 0.208 ns for an input-to-output path and about 0.5 ns for input-to-register paths.
findings.action: Add an interface timing contract: every output from a flop, no combinational input-to-output path, and a stated budget per port group.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: Reset is used as handshake data and nothing forbids it
findings.detail: The RTL derives the ready and valid enable directly from the reset pin in profiles 0 and 1 (w_handshake_active = i_rst_n_cluster, tile_coh_adapter.sv:136 and axi_route.sv:425); only profile 2 registers the release (§8.3). The report shows i_rst_n_cluster as the start point of an input-to-register path (-2.16 ns) and of an input-to-output path (-0.60 ns).
findings.action: Add a rule that the reset port never appears in a ready or valid expression, and register the release in every profile.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: REQ-PERF-007 is untraced and its tests run only profile 1
findings.detail: REQ-PERF-007 cites TEST-057 to TEST-061 on profiles 0 and 2, but the five tests are written for profile 1 and §19 has no row for REQ-PERF-007.
findings.action: Parameterize the five tests over profiles 0, 1 and 2 and add the REQ-PERF-007 row.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: Parameter table lists two timing profiles; RTL and §8.3 use three
findings.detail: §8.1 gives PARA_TIMING_PROFILE as 0 or 1 while §8.3, DEC-045 and RTL (LPARA_TIMING_PROFILE_BOUNDARY = 2) define profile 2; the RTL also adds PARA_DIR_SYNC_READ, driven from profile 2, which no section documents.
findings.action: Update the §8.1 legal range and document PARA_DIR_SYNC_READ as internal or public.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: Directory storage is inline flops, not a macro-replaceable RAM
findings.detail: §8.3 says the directory uses synchronous 1RW storage per way with macro mapping left to synthesis, but the RTL keeps the arrays as reg_entry inside m_vlsit_riscv_sharer_directory with no RAM module boundary; synthesis maps them to 206,600 flops (74 percent of 280,306) and 2.82 mm2 (56 percent of 4.998 mm2).
findings.action: Add a RAM wrapper module with a fixed interface and keep valid, PLRU and reservation in flops.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: No area or power proxy although a mapped number exists
findings.detail: §13 states that no area or power figure is available. The synthesis report gives a mapped number (ARM sc12 55LPx RVT, ss_nominal_max_1p08v_125c, Design Compiler X-2025.06-SP5): 4.998 mm2 and 280,250 sequential cells for two harts, with every SRAM macro excluded.
findings.action: Record a proxy table (flip-flop counts per block, storage bits) and the mapped number with its library and corner.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: Performance is stated as cases and formulas with no value
findings.detail: Every row of the §13 table is qualitative, the profiles add 'registered latency' with no cycle count, and TEST-046 only reports observed values.
findings.action: Add measured cycles for hit, clean miss, dirty-owner transfer and CBO, and the latency delta of each profile.

findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.title: Gateway DMA depends on 16-byte CBO with no throughput budget
findings.detail: The application hands network buffers to non-coherent DMA through per-line CBO operations on 16-byte lines (FEAT-010); a 1500-byte packet needs about 94 operations, each a serialized CCU transaction, and no section gives a rate requirement or a limit on this cost.
findings.action: Add a CBO throughput requirement or decide an I/O-coherent port (OPEN-ACE-MAP).

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: External interrupt to CVA6 mapping is not specified
findings.detail: The interface table names per-hart MEIP and SEIP inputs and TEST-013 checks only that each vector reaches the addressed hart; no requirement ties i_int_meip to mip.MEIP and i_int_seip to mip.SEIP. The RTL had the two swapped at the CVA6 boundary (irq_i); the current source carries a correction.
findings.action: Add the mapping requirement and a test of mip.MEIP, mip.SEIP, delegation and WFI wake-up.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: No version or configuration register and no hart start control
findings.detail: §11.5 records that the ABI has no version register at offset zero; firmware cannot read the hart count, the profile or the LLC geometry, and REQ-SYS-003 starts all harts at one boot address so software must park them by mhartid.
findings.action: Add a read-only version and configuration register and decide whether a hart-start control is in scope.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: No elaboration-time legality check of parameters
findings.detail: REQ-SYS-001 says the cluster shall elaborate only for 2 or 4 harts, but no source under rtl/non_coherence_cluster or rtl/common/vlsit/{cpu,coherence} contains an elaboration error, and the active-hart masks treat any value other than 2 as 4.
findings.action: Add generate-time checks for every §8.1 parameter.

findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.title: Atomic probe-slot claim can starve a wide-mask context
findings.detail: A PREPARE context is granted only when every slot in its mask is free; narrow contexts can claim single slots again and again, so a context needing three or four slots may never find them all free; the round-robin pointer orders contexts but does not reserve slots, and TEST-056 covers one two-context case.
findings.action: Add an aging rule and a fairness property for the wide-mask claim.

findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.title: Directory capacity equals the L1 D-cache capacity
findings.detail: The directory holds PARA_CPU_NUM x 2,048 entries, the same count as the private D-cache lines; any set conflict forces a replacement that invalidates a live L1 line, and stale-positive holders (REQ-MEM-008) occupy entries, yet no section quantifies the extra invalidations.
findings.action: Measure conflict invalidations and decide an over-provision factor, now cheap once the storage is a RAM.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: No ECC or parity decision for L1, LLC and directory
findings.detail: §18 makes ECC depend on macros and tool flow, the selected CVA6 configuration sets DcacheEccEnable to 0, and an industrial gateway is the stated application; a detected memory error has no defined path other than the reset-only fatal record.
findings.action: Decide ECC or parity per array and record the error response.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: No timeout and reset-only recovery: one stuck hart stops the cluster
findings.detail: PREPARE, COMMIT and ABORT have no acknowledgement timeout (REQ-MEM-013); an ordinary dirty-eviction error is recoverable only by reset (REQ-ERR-003); there is no per-hart reset, so a missing response holds a slot and line lock until the whole cluster resets.
findings.action: Keep the approved decision and require a SoC watchdog that resets the cluster.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: All DFT is delegated to the SoC and the top has no test port
findings.detail: §16 leaves scan, MBIST and ATPG to the SoC; the top exposes no scan or test-enable port, the LLC test enable is tied to zero (cluster_core.sv:93, 967), the flow uses automatic clock gating with PREICG cells, and §16 requires test-enable behavior for any gating without defining the port.
findings.action: Define the DFT hand-off: test-enable port, scan clock and reset handling, MBIST interface for L1, LLC and directory RAM.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: PPROT and debug authorization policy undecided
findings.detail: §18 states PPROT handling must be configured explicitly but no decision exists, so any AXI4-Lite master can flush the LLC or change the PMU; DEP-006 leaves debug authorization to the SoC.
findings.action: Choose a PPROT rule for the control windows.

findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.title: Debug specification revision is 0.13.2
findings.detail: REF-007 pins the RISC-V Debug Specification 0.13.2, while a later ratified 1.0 revision adds halt groups and per-hart reset; the specification does not say which later features are out of scope.
findings.action: State the revision basis and the excluded features.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: 31 open items without owner or date; a 9.7k-line single document
findings.detail: The inventory finds 31 open items (ASM-001 to ASM-007, DEP-001 to DEP-025) with a status text but no owner or due date; the document is about 9,700 lines, and the revision history sits only in the preface.
findings.action: Add owner and date columns and a revision table.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: No named properties and no coverage threshold
findings.detail: The inventory finds no property identifiers; §15.3 lists required assertions in prose and states that coverage thresholds are not yet selected, while §15.4 names formal and liveness analyses with no property list.
findings.action: Assign PROP identifiers, link them to requirements and set the coverage thresholds.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: Features marked Required are verified by lint only
findings.detail: OPEN-DV lists PMU, native LLC service, MMIO and uncached ATOP, IRQ, debug and WFI and random coherence as not yet functionally closed; the earlier interrupt swap and the LLC bridge double response were in exactly these areas.
findings.action: Make a functional test a sign-off condition for each Required feature.

findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.title: No rule that a halted or WFI hart still answers probes
findings.detail: §7.4 only says WFI behavior must be checked against CVA6; because probes have no timeout, a hart whose cache clock is gated in WFI or whose cache stops in debug halt would hold every line it owns and hang the cluster.
findings.action: Add a requirement that the cache and probe endpoint stay clocked and responsive in WFI and debug halt.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: Deferred ACE configurations sit in the active tables
findings.detail: CFG-ACE-2, CFG-ACE-4, FEAT-005, REQ-IF-004 and TEST-008 are in the same tables as the implemented configurations although the ACE profile is not part of this RTL phase.
findings.action: Mark the ACE rows as deferred in a Status column.

findings.label: INFERENCE
findings.title: Compared with commercial clusters: no I/O coherence, no L2 ECC, no frequency claim
findings.detail: Press coverage dated 2020 describes the Andes AX45MP cluster as up to four cores with a MESI coherence manager, an L2 cache and I/O coherence for cacheless masters, at about 2.4 GHz in 12 nm; the SiFive U74-MC is described as four U74 cores plus a monitor core with a 2 MB L2 with ECC. This IP has an internal MESI domain and a shared LLC but no external coherent port, no ECC decision and no frequency evidence.
findings.action: Decide the I/O-coherent port and the ECC level for the target market.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: SoC obligations are scattered with no integration checklist
findings.detail: The integrator must provide a synchronized reset release, a coordinated fabric reset, an atomic-capable AXI target, software cache maintenance for DMA, SRAM views, SDC, an interrupt mapping and a Debug Module; each appears in a different section.
findings.action: Add one integration checklist section.

findings.label: FACT
findings.title: Circular-wait risk of the per-hart probe slot is closed in the specification
findings.detail: REQ-MEM-024 and DEC-043 require all expected slots to be claimed atomically before any probe is issued, with assertions in §15.3 and TEST-056; this closes the wait cycle between two contexts that each held one hart slot and needed the other's.
findings.action: Keep it; add the fairness rule of F-013.
